title: Aston Martin Valhalla Spider: the ultimate open-top supercar
extract: Aston Martin's Valhalla Spider pairs a removable fabric roof with the Valhalla's 1,079PS plug-in-hybrid powertrain: an 828PS 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 plus three electric motors. Revised aerodynamics and stability calibrations preserve the 217mph top speed with the roof removed or the optional carbon-fibre hardtop fitted.

title: This Audi Quattro Restomod Swaps Its Famous Five-Cylinder for a 10,000-RPM V8
extract: The British-built Audacious IV uses B7 RS4 underpinnings, a 4.2-litre V8, Torsen all-wheel drive and a six-speed manual in a Quattro-inspired body. Four power configurations include two versions capable of 10,000rpm; the most powerful supercharged setup is rated at 750hp, with production limited to 50 cars.

title: Mistral AI publicly releases Large 4, targets cybersecurity users
extract: Mistral publicly released Large 4, an open-weight model designed to help organisations identify and fix cybersecurity vulnerabilities. It can be downloaded and run on an organisation's own systems, and was upgraded after testing with government and corporate users.

title: AI found a way to crash bitcoin nodes on Windows and Macs. It's now public
extract: A language-model scan uncovered three Bitcoin Core flaws, including a remote memory-exhaustion bug that could crash nodes on Windows, macOS and BSD. Human contributors verified the findings, fixes shipped on 27 October, and the project disclosed them under a new policy for bugs that AI tools can readily discover.

title: Attackers turn GitHub issues into supply chain campaign against 61 public repos in less than an hour
extract: Radware identified 83 malicious issues, pull requests or comments across 61 public GitHub repositories, including LangExtract, Trivy, Brave and MLflow. Hidden HTML comments triggered vulnerable CI workflows to execute commands and attempt to exfiltrate secrets; researchers confirmed two executions but could not establish whether credentials were stolen.

title: Researchers find bugs in 5 AI developer tools, with OpenAI and Microsoft flaws still unpatched
extract: Researchers found vulnerabilities in Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude Desktop, VS Code and Codex. The common weakness was embedded browsers with excessive capabilities, potentially enabling host command execution, local file access or address-bar spoofing; The Register reported that the Codex and VS Code issues remained unpatched at publication.

title: Topcoat enables Rust to render server-side web apps
extract: AWS engineer Carl Lerche, creator of Tokio, presented Topcoat, a Rust framework for server-rendered web apps. It compiles Rust into browser-friendly JavaScript while keeping most application logic on the server, aiming to reduce client-side loading overhead for conventional database-driven sites.

title: Startup wants to make AI agents safe for DevOps duty
extract: University of Michigan researchers founded Vera Platforms to benchmark and train AI agents for production DevOps tasks. Its CloudOpsBench test includes S3 bucket cleanup, compliance-pipeline repair and DynamoDB autoscaling, using a simulator to test agents before they touch live infrastructure.

title: Attention Seeking Behaviour by Aea Varfis-van Warmelo review – a slippery liar’s tale
extract: A Goldsmiths-shortlisted debut follows an unreliable narrator who compulsively lies, then becomes entangled in copying legal files for a journalist investigating a rape case. The review praises its unsettling questions about memory, credibility and justice, while noting that a digression into facial-action coding interrupts the narrative.

title: Bram Stoker’s Dracula audiobook review – cinematic horror with an A-list cast
extract: Mary Lambert's Audible Originals adaptation, adapted by Robyn Ahern, gives Bram Stoker's novel cinematic sound design and a cast led by Jonathan Bailey, Ella Purnell, Aimee Lou Wood and Maggie Gyllenhaal. The Guardian praises its immersive audio effects and streamlined retelling, which avoids camp while retaining shocks and gore.

title: The best recent translated fiction – review roundup
extract: The Guardian reviews four translations: Barbi Marković's surreal, darkly comic Minihorror; Pol Guasch's climate-changed Paradise Burns; Helle Helle's Danish road-trip novel Hafni Says; and Hamid Ismailov's action-filled, darkly funny stories Googling for Soul.

title: Philippa Gregory: I read 100 of the 18th century’s most popular novels – the perfect author’s apprenticeship
extract: Historical novelist Philippa Gregory explains how reading more than 100 popular 18th-century novels for her PhD became an apprenticeship in plot, structure and character. She discusses influences from Jane Austen and Elizabeth Goudge to Dickens and Iris Murdoch, and how those books shaped her approach to historical fiction.

title: I Love Boosters review – supercool outlaw women go shoplifting in Boots Riley’s frantic and funny caper
extract: Boots Riley's fashion-industry fantasy-caper follows three outlaw women who steal couture and resell it cheaply, only to encounter a rival using a magical portal ring. The Guardian finds it funny and imaginative, though its relentless pace can become exhausting.

title: Basketweavers get in a twist over Alexander Skarsgård’s Wicker Husband
extract: The film's wicker-clad character has prompted a debate among basket makers over willow, plaiting and traditional weaving. Wētā Workshop's team built the costume from 50 interlocking 3D-printed thermoplastic pieces attached to a suit, choosing the material for movement rather than traditional basketry.

title: The Mosquito Bowl review – Netflix mixes football, war and cliches in slick by-the-numbers saga
extract: Peter Berg's Netflix drama follows four college football stars who join the US Marines after Pearl Harbor and culminates in a 1944 Christmas Eve game at Guadalcanal. The Guardian finds the football and battle sequences absorbing but criticises its thin characterisation and familiar patriotic clichés.

title: Elke Sommer, prolific German star of A Shot in the Dark and And Then There Were None, dies aged 85
extract: The German-born actor became a familiar face in 1960s and 70s cinema, appearing opposite Peter Sellers in A Shot in the Dark, in Agatha Christie's And Then There Were None and in Carry On Behind. The obituary also recalls her Hollywood comedies and cult horror films for Mario Bava.

title: Susan Saint James obituary
extract: The US actor starred opposite Rock Hudson in McMillan & Wife before becoming one half of the sitcom Kate & Allie. The obituary covers her two decades of television work, including crime drama, comedy and later guest roles.

title: Sir Patrick Stewart obituary
extract: The obituary traces Stewart's career from the Royal Shakespeare Company to global fame as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Professor Charles Xavier in X-Men. It also recalls his roles in Dune, I, Claudius, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, Extras and Frasier, alongside a long stage career.

title: Ferrari’s new patent: why Maranello is putting a roof scoop on supercars
extract: A Ferrari patent describes a roof-mounted intake and duct to route hot air from the front radiator away from the rear wing. The proposed system is intended to keep the wing working in cleaner airflow; the patent does not establish that the design will reach production or quantify any downforce gain.

title: Google’s first data center satellite is online and writing poetry
extract: Google’s Suncatcher prototype has reached orbit and is communicating with the ground. The test satellite carries four Google TPUs and a roughly one-kilowatt solar power system, putting the company’s idea of space-based AI computing into an early hardware-testing phase.

title: Can AI data centers be mass-produced like cars? This startup aims to find out
extract: Runware is developing a factory approach to modular AI data centers, assembling prefabricated computing pods rather than building each facility as a bespoke project. The company says its process can manufacture and deliver a dense computing pod in as little as 48 hours.

title: Granola crunches up a dictation feature to compete with Wispr
extract: Meeting-notes app Granola has added a Mac dictation feature that can be invoked with the Fn key. It transcribes speech and cleans up the wording for use across applications, extending the product beyond its original meeting-notes workflow.

title: Ex-Palantir execs launch Dream with $17M from a16z to build AI world models for construction
extract: Startup Dream is applying AI world models to construction and architecture, engineering and construction workflows. Its systems are intended to simulate physical environments and building constraints, potentially giving designers and contractors a way to test proposed changes before work begins.

title: Waymo taps Toyota to supply robotaxis for Japan and the UK
extract: Waymo is working with Toyota on a robotaxi programme built around the bZ4X, with Japan and the UK among the markets in view. The partnership is a notable step in taking Waymo’s autonomous-driving system beyond its existing vehicle and operating-market footprint.

title: North Korean hackers blamed for stealing record $6.3B in Binance breach
extract: Investigators have attributed a record-breaking cryptocurrency theft affecting Binance to North Korean hackers. The report describes the scale of the alleged loss, efforts to freeze funds and how compromise of an engineer’s laptop formed part of the attack chain.

title: DoorDash said it’s only received ‘several hundred’ orders from AI agents
extract: DoorDash executives said the company has received only several hundred orders placed by third-party AI agents, a tiny number beside the millions of daily deliveries handled through its service. The comments offer a reality check on how much agent-driven commerce is happening in practice.

title: LibreOffice’s ‘no AI’ stance meets LLM-assisted code
extract: The Document Foundation says LibreOffice has no built-in AI features and its core developers do not use LLMs, while community contributors may use coding assistants if they disclose that use and their submissions receive careful review. The report explores the distinction between an AI-free product and an AI-free development process.

title: Foo Fighters close ‘Kimmel’ run with a trip down ‘Baker Street’
extract: Foo Fighters revisited their 1997 cover of Gerry Rafferty’s ‘Baker Street’ during their run on Jimmy Kimmel Live. The performance brings a rarely played track from the band’s early catalogue back into the spotlight.

title: 90 New Sci-Fi, Fantasy, and Horror Books Arriving in November
extract: Gizmodo previews a large slate of November science-fiction, fantasy and horror releases, including new work from John Scalzi, Cassandra Khaw and other genre writers. The roundup is a useful look ahead at the month’s speculative-fiction reading, alongside memoirs from genre favourites.

title: ‘I left shellshocked’: writers on their scariest non-horror movies
extract: Writers pick films that frightened them without belonging to the horror genre, ranging from classic animation and science fiction to unsettling dramas and thrillers. The selection looks at the ways atmosphere, imagery and ideas can be more disturbing than conventional horror shocks.

title: John Carpenter says answer to The Thing’s ending is hiding in the movie
extract: John Carpenter has said that the solution to the famously ambiguous ending of his 1982 science-fiction horror film The Thing is visible within the movie itself. The filmmaker maintains that audiences have not yet identified the clue he has in mind, renewing discussion around one of the genre’s enduring mysteries.

title: From Possible Love to Ali G: Who Iz I?: the seven best films to watch on TV this week
extract: The Guardian’s weekly television-film selection ranges from comedy to documentary and genre cinema, including Ali G: Who Iz I?, The Fog and Talk to Me. It is a compact guide to the films scheduled for television during the coming week.
